name: Visualization Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on visualization so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on visualization so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any visualization bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. When multiple visualization strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Keep visualization outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to visualization (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. When visualization guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Keep visualization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen visualization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. State assumptions about visualization explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
9. Before starting visualization work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic visualization advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated visualization concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of visualization correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about visualization over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
